metadata.research_goal: Create a backend-ready research draft for association football rules, match structure, pitch zones, formations, phases of play, restarts, tactical constraints, physical demands, injury/load risks, and beginner/intermediate/advanced teaching implications.
metadata.edition_note: IFAB latest pages accessed during research list the 2026/27 and 2025/26 law sets. Production rules should store a competition_law_edition field and verify the exact edition used by each target competition.
metadata.scope_note: Association football/soccer 11v11 is primary. Adaptations are needed for small-sided youth formats, futsal, beach soccer, and local competition modifications.

key_concepts.name: Objective and scoring
key_concepts.summary: A match is won by the team scoring more goals. A goal requires the whole ball to cross the goal line between posts and under the crossbar with no prior attacking offence.
key_concepts.coaching_use: Teach attackers to finish across the line, defenders and goalkeepers to protect the goal line, and players to keep playing until the referee signals.

levels.beginner: Recognise a goal and restart after a goal.
levels.intermediate: Understand line decisions, advantage, and why play may continue after partial ball crossing.
levels.advanced: Connect goal-line moments with pressing the rebound, VAR/GLT context, and defensive covering positions.

key_concepts.name: Field geometry and legal boundaries
key_concepts.summary: The field is rectangular, touchlines are longer than goal lines, the lines belong to the areas they bound, and international matches use a narrower dimension range than the general law range.
key_concepts.coaching_use: Link line ownership to penalty-area fouls, ball-in/out decisions, throw-in placement, wide play, and pressure near boundaries.

levels.beginner: Know touchlines, goal lines, halfway line, penalty area, goal area, and corner arcs.
levels.intermediate: Use boundaries as tactical constraints for pressing traps and build-out spacing.
levels.advanced: Model pitch size effects on team compactness, pressing distances, crossing zones, and transition exposure.

key_concepts.name: Thirds, wide channels, central lane, and half-spaces
key_concepts.summary: Thirds and channels are coaching models rather than IFAB field markings. Teams commonly describe defensive, middle, and attacking thirds, plus wide channels, central lane, and inside channels/half-spaces to organise possession, pressing, and chance creation.
key_concepts.coaching_use: Use zones to teach where to build, progress, create, press, recover, and protect central access.

levels.beginner: Name defensive, middle, and attacking thirds.
levels.intermediate: Recognise when to play wide, inside, backward, or forward based on pressure.
levels.advanced: Manipulate overloads and isolations by shifting occupation across channels and lines.

key_concepts.name: Players and substitutions
key_concepts.summary: A standard match has two teams with up to eleven players each, one being the goalkeeper; a match cannot start or continue with fewer than seven players on either team. Official competition substitution numbers are set by competition rules within IFAB limits.
key_concepts.coaching_use: Tie substitution planning to tactical changes, fatigue management, injury response, card risk, extra time, and role coverage.

levels.beginner: Know that each team has eleven players including a goalkeeper.
levels.intermediate: Understand substitute timing and why repeated stoppages are limited.
levels.advanced: Plan substitution windows around match state, pressing intensity, set-piece roles, and extra-time probability.

key_concepts.name: Match clock and added time
key_concepts.summary: Adult 11v11 matches are two equal 45-minute halves unless lawfully reduced, with a half-time interval not exceeding 15 minutes and referee allowance for time lost.
key_concepts.coaching_use: Teach game management: tempo control, restart urgency, energy pacing, tactical fouling risk, and late-match decision-making.

levels.beginner: Know halves, half-time, and that the referee adds time.
levels.intermediate: Recognise time-wasting and restart delay consequences.
levels.advanced: Prepare late-game and added-time tactical plans that balance scoreline, fatigue, and sanction risk.

key_concepts.name: Extra time and penalty shoot-out
key_concepts.summary: Where competition rules require a winner after a draw, permitted methods include extra time of two equal periods not exceeding 15 minutes each, penalties, away goals, or combinations allowed by competition rules.
key_concepts.coaching_use: Prepare tactical and physical plans for fatigue, substitution timing, penalty taker order, goalkeeper replacement options, and psychological readiness.

levels.beginner: Know that knockout games may continue after 90 minutes.
levels.intermediate: Understand extra-time periods and shoot-out eligibility basics.
levels.advanced: Model substitution and penalty-order decisions before full-time based on player load, composure, injury status, and goalkeeper strategy.

key_concepts.name: Ball in and out of play
key_concepts.summary: The ball is out only when it wholly crosses a boundary, play is stopped by the referee, or specific match-official contact conditions occur. Otherwise, rebounds from goalposts, crossbar, corner flags, and officials usually remain live unless the law states otherwise.
key_concepts.coaching_use: Train players to continue actions until the whistle or clear ball-out decision and to react first to live rebounds.

levels.intermediate: React to rebounds and referee-contact restarts.
levels.advanced: Use boundary pressure and second-ball positioning to win restarts or regain possession.

key_concepts.name: Restart taxonomy
key_concepts.summary: Restarts include kick-off, dropped ball, direct free kick, indirect free kick, penalty kick, throw-in, goal kick, and corner kick. Each restart has a location, spacing, ball-in-play condition, and scoring possibility.
key_concepts.coaching_use: Build a restart library for attacking routines, defensive organisation, quick-restart awareness, and referee-management education.

levels.beginner: Identify the common restart after ball out or foul.
levels.intermediate: Know direct/indirect free kick and set-piece spacing.
levels.advanced: Design phase-specific restart routines and transition protections after failed set pieces.

key_concepts.name: Offside as a space-time constraint
key_concepts.summary: Being in an offside position is not itself an offence; the player is penalised only when involved in active play from a team-mate's play/touch while nearer to the opponents' goal line than both the ball and second-last opponent in the opponents' half.
key_concepts.coaching_use: Teach timed runs, line-breaking passes, defensive-line control, goalkeeper sweeper decisions, and no-offside restart opportunities.

levels.beginner: Know why forwards cannot simply wait behind defenders.
levels.intermediate: Time runs from onside positions and recognise no-offside restarts.
levels.advanced: Manipulate the defensive line with blindside runs, third-player movements, delayed passes, and high-line pressing.

key_concepts.name: Fouls, cards, and contact thresholds
key_concepts.summary: Direct free kick offences include contact actions judged careless, reckless, or using excessive force. Careless contact normally has no card, reckless contact is cautioned, and excessive force or endangering safety is a send-off.
key_concepts.coaching_use: Train duel technique, tackle selection, pressing body shape, card-risk decisions, and how fouls change tactical context.

levels.beginner: Avoid pushing, tripping, kicking, and handling the ball.
levels.intermediate: Differentiate fair challenge, careless foul, reckless foul, and dangerous play.
levels.advanced: Manage tactical foul risk, DOGSO/stopping-promising-attack exposure, and pressing intensity near penalty areas.

key_concepts.name: Handball and goalkeeper handling
key_concepts.summary: Not every hand/arm contact is an offence. Deliberate handling, making the body unnaturally bigger, and scoring directly or immediately from the hand/arm are key offence categories. Goalkeepers have special handling privileges only inside their penalty area and face restrictions on back-passes, throw-ins from team-mates, second touches, and time in possession.
key_concepts.coaching_use: Teach defenders arm position, blockers body shape, goalkeeper distribution speed, and build-out choices after back-passes.

levels.beginner: Outfield players should not use hands/arms to play the ball.
levels.intermediate: Understand deliberate handling and unnatural body shape.
levels.advanced: Connect handball risk to shot-block technique, penalty-area defending, and goalkeeper build-up under pressure.

key_concepts.name: Formation as starting structure, not fixed behaviour
key_concepts.summary: Formations describe nominal player distribution, but teams often have different attacking, defensive, and transition shapes. The same 4-3-3 can become a 3-2-5 in possession, a 4-1-4-1 press, or a 4-5-1 block depending on player roles and match plan.
key_concepts.coaching_use: Separate team shape from player tasks: spacing, pressing responsibility, rest defence, support angles, and transition jobs.

levels.beginner: Learn goalkeeper, defenders, midfielders, and forwards.
levels.intermediate: Understand role numbers and lines within common formations.
levels.advanced: Teach formation morphing by phase and how roles interact with opponent structure.

key_concepts.name: Phases of play
key_concepts.summary: A practical game model separates in possession, out of possession, transition to attack, transition to defend, and set pieces. FIFA EFI further distinguishes attacking phases such as build-up, progression, final third, and counter-attack.
key_concepts.coaching_use: Map every drill and match behaviour to a phase, then assess the decisions and physical actions demanded by that phase.

levels.intermediate: Identify build-up, progression, final third, press, block, and transition.
levels.advanced: Use phase-specific KPIs such as regain height, counter-attack time, line breaks, box entries, and rest-defence balance.

key_concepts.name: Transition moments
key_concepts.summary: The first seconds after losing or regaining the ball often determine whether a team can create a high-quality chance or prevent one. Teams generally choose between immediate counter-pressing and recovering into a compact defensive shape after loss.
key_concepts.coaching_use: Train nearest-player pressure, cover, compactness, counter-attack recognition, first forward pass, and safe possession after regain.

levels.intermediate: Learn press, cover, recover, and first-pass options.
levels.advanced: Design counter-press traps, rest-defence structures, and fast vertical attacks based on opponent shape.

key_concepts.name: Style of play
key_concepts.summary: A style of play expresses a team's intended behaviour in attack, defence, and transition. It should be specific enough to guide coaching decisions but flexible enough to adapt to players, opponent, match state, and rules.
key_concepts.coaching_use: Translate rules and phase models into team principles, role expectations, session design, and assessment language.

levels.beginner: Use simple identity statements such as keep the ball, win it back, or attack quickly.
levels.intermediate: Connect style to formations and training themes.
levels.advanced: Build a complete game model with principles, sub-principles, constraints, and match-state adaptations.

key_concepts.name: Physical game model
key_concepts.summary: Football is intermittent: players alternate walking, jogging, accelerations, decelerations, duels, jumps, high-speed runs, sprints, and recovery periods over 90 minutes plus added time and possibly extra time.
key_concepts.coaching_use: Design practices that reflect the tactical context of running rather than only generic distance totals.

levels.beginner: Build general movement quality and ability to repeat efforts.
levels.intermediate: Connect fitness to pressing, recovering, overlapping, and counter-attacking.
levels.advanced: Benchmark high-intensity, sprint, acceleration, deceleration, positional, and phase-specific load.

technical_models.name: Core IFAB Law Constraint Model
technical_models.purpose: Represent law constraints that directly shape match structure, tactical choices, and teaching content.

core_constraints.value: 11 per team, one must be goalkeeper
core_constraints.impact: Shapes 1v1, unit, line, and team balance; creates special goalkeeper role.

core_constraints.value: Match may not start or continue if either team has fewer than seven players
core_constraints.impact: Red cards can make match continuation impossible and drastically alter tactics before that threshold.

core_constraints.value: General range 90-120 m long and 45-90 m wide; international range 100-110 m long and 64-75 m wide
core_constraints.impact: Wider/larger fields reward spacing and running capacity; smaller fields compress decisions and pressing distances.

core_constraints.value: Two equal halves of 45 minutes plus allowance for time lost
core_constraints.impact: Requires pacing, substitutions, late-game management, and recovery planning.

core_constraints.value: Whole ball over goal line between posts and under crossbar with no scoring-team offence
core_constraints.impact: Supports goal-line defending, rebound behaviour, and technology use where available.

core_constraints.value: Applies to active involvement from an offside position in opponents' half, with no offence directly from goal kick, throw-in, or corner kick
core_constraints.impact: Creates defensive line tactics, run timing, passing lanes, and restart opportunities.

core_constraints.value: Careless, reckless, and excessive-force thresholds determine free kick, caution, or send-off
core_constraints.impact: Constrains pressing and tackling aggressiveness, especially near the penalty area and when already cautioned.

core_constraints.value: Competition rules set numbers; top-level five-substitute format uses three opportunities plus half-time, with extra-time provisions
core_constraints.impact: Creates tactical timing constraints and changes how coaches manage fatigue, injuries, role matchups, and card risk.

technical_models.name: Pitch Zones and Tactical Geography Model
technical_models.purpose: Map official areas and coaching zones into reusable tactical teaching locations.

official_areas.law_detail: Extends 5.5 m from inside of each goalpost and 5.5 m into the field
official_areas.coaching_meaning: Goal kicks can be taken from anywhere inside; goalkeeper restart positioning and short build-up starts here.

official_areas.law_detail: Extends 16.5 m from inside of each goalpost and 16.5 m into the field; penalty mark 11 m from midpoint between posts
official_areas.coaching_meaning: Direct free kick offences by defenders here become penalties; defensive duel technique and arm position are critical.

official_areas.law_detail: Quarter circle of 1 m radius from each corner flagpost
official_areas.coaching_meaning: Corner routines and short-corner spacing begin here.

official_areas.law_detail: Whole ball must cross the line to be out; lines belong to the areas they bound
official_areas.coaching_meaning: Boundary pressure can trap opponents; line ownership matters for penalty-area decisions.

primary_team_tasks: build from goalkeeper and back line
win and defend attacking set pieces
connect winger, full-back, midfielder, and striker

technical_models.name: Match Timing and Outcome Model
technical_models.purpose: Represent normal time, added time, extra time, and penalties as state transitions.

states.duration: not exceeding 15 minutes unless lawfully altered
coaching_tasks: make substitutions without using a substitution opportunity where competition rules allow

states.duration: two equal periods not exceeding 15 minutes each when competition rules require a winner

coaching_tasks: manage equalised player numbers after send-offs

technical_models.name: Phase of Play Model
technical_models.purpose: Classify team behaviour by possession state and tactical objective.

phases.objective: Initiate attack and progress away from own goal under low, medium, or high pressure.
rule_constraints: goal-kick ball in play when kicked and clearly moves
opponents outside penalty area at goal kick until ball in play
goalkeeper handling restrictions after team-mate back-pass

phases.objective: Break one or more opposition lines with pass, carry, combination, switch, or third-player movement.
rule_constraints: offside timing for forward receivers
foul/contact risk while shielding
boundary restart risk near touchline

phases.objective: Create and finish chances while keeping balance for the next transition.
rule_constraints: offside line
penalty-area foul consequences
handball and contact discipline
corner and throw-in restart opportunities

phases.objective: Exploit opponent disorganisation or secure possession if forward play is not available.
player_tasks: secure if counter-press pressure is strong
rule_constraints: offside only from team-mate play/touch
no offside from goal kick, throw-in, or corner
advantage after fouls can allow attack to continue

phases.objective: Prevent clean build-up, force mistakes, or regain near goal.
rule_constraints: contact thresholds
failing to respect restart distance
offside line behind press

phases.objective: Control central space, protect goal, force play outside, and prepare counter-attack.
rule_constraints: penalty-area foul risk
offside line depth
corner and free-kick concession risk

phases.typical_location: any third, highest risk when own team is expanded
phases.objective: Either counter-press immediately or recover into defensive shape to prevent opponent progression.
rule_constraints: foul/caution risk for stopping promising attacks
offside line can help compactness but creates space behind
advantage may punish late tactical fouls

phases.objective: Exploit or defend structured restarts and organise the next transition.
rule_constraints: opponent distance
ball stationary or thrown correctly
direct/indirect scoring rules
second-touch restrictions

technical_models.name: Restart Decision and Teaching Model
technical_models.purpose: Store restart type, trigger, location, ball-in-play condition, scoring constraints, opponent spacing, and tactical implications.

restarts.trigger: start of each half, each extra-time period, and after a goal
restarts.opponent_distance: 9.15 m until ball is in play
restarts.teaching_note: Use kick-off to establish first possession plan and immediate counterpress coverage.

restarts.trigger: referee stops play and no other restart is required, including specified match-official contact cases
restarts.location: where play was stopped or interference/contact occurred, with goalkeeper drop in defending penalty area when applicable
restarts.direct_goal_allowed: no direct goal unless at least two players touch before goal
restarts.teaching_note: Teach awareness after referee stoppages and fair but alert positioning.

restarts.trigger: direct free kick offence or applicable handball/contact misconduct
restarts.location: generally where offence occurred, with law-specific exceptions
restarts.opponent_distance: 9.15 m unless on own goal line between posts
restarts.ball_live_when: stationary ball is kicked and clearly moves
restarts.teaching_note: Train quick free kicks, shooting routines, crossing routines, and counter-rest defence.

restarts.trigger: indirect offences including offside, dangerous play, impeding without contact, goalkeeper handling restrictions, and some procedural offences
restarts.location: where offence occurred, with goal-area and law-specific exceptions
restarts.opponent_distance: 9.15 m unless on own goal line between posts
restarts.ball_live_when: stationary ball is kicked and clearly moves
restarts.direct_goal_allowed: no; another player must touch before goal can count
restarts.teaching_note: Teach signal recognition and second-touch routines.

restarts.trigger: direct free kick offence by a player inside own penalty area or off-field offence treated under Laws 12 and 13
restarts.opponent_distance: all players except kicker and goalkeeper at least 9.15 m from mark, outside penalty area, behind mark, inside field
restarts.teaching_note: Train taker routine, goalkeeper behaviour, encroachment awareness, and rebound responsibility.

restarts.trigger: whole ball crosses touchline after last touch by opponent, on ground or in air
restarts.teaching_note: Use as possession restart, pressing trigger, or territorial gain; teach legal mechanics and second-touch rule.

restarts.trigger: whole ball crosses goal line after last touch by attacking team and no goal is scored
restarts.location: any point in the defending team's goal area
restarts.opponent_distance: opponents outside penalty area until ball is in play
restarts.teaching_note: Teach short build-up, long distribution, press-resistance, and risk management near own goal.

restarts.trigger: whole ball crosses goal line after last touch by defending team and no goal is scored; latest IFAB language also includes specified goalkeeper-control and delayed goal-kick sanctions
restarts.location: nearest corner area or specified goalkeeper position when applicable
restarts.opponent_distance: 9.15 m from corner arc until ball is in play
restarts.teaching_note: Teach delivery, blocking within law, box occupation, second balls, and transition defence.

season_sensitive_details: The latest IFAB pages include throw-in and goal-kick countdown protocol language and goalkeeper-control sanctions that should be validated against the competition law edition before production enforcement.

technical_models.name: Offside Tactical Constraint Model
technical_models.purpose: Translate Law 11 into teachable attacking and defending decisions.

decision_nodes.question: At the moment of team-mate play/touch, is any playable body part in the opponents' half and nearer to the goal line than both the ball and second-last opponent?
Does the player interfere with play, interfere with an opponent, or gain an advantage from rebound/deflection/save?
decision_nodes.if_no: No offence simply for being in the position.
decision_nodes.if_yes: Indirect free kick where offence occurred.

decision_nodes.question: Did the player receive directly from goal kick, throw-in, or corner?
decision_nodes.if_yes: No offside offence from that direct receipt.

decision_nodes.question: Did an opponent deliberately play the ball with control and possibility to pass, possess, or clear, excluding deliberate saves?
decision_nodes.if_yes: Offside attacker is not considered to have gained advantage solely from that deliberate play.

tactical_effects: Attacking teams time runs and passes to exploit depth without early occupation.
Defensive teams use line height to compress space but must manage runs behind.
Goalkeepers become sweepers when the defensive line is high.
No-offside restarts create throw-in, goal-kick, and corner-specific attacking possibilities.

technical_models.name: Fouls, Misconduct, and Card Risk Model
technical_models.purpose: Connect foul categories to tactical and coaching decisions.

severity_ladder.typical_sanction: direct free kick or penalty if inside offender's penalty area
severity_ladder.coaching_message: Improve body position, timing, and control.
Reduce uncontrolled speed and late contact, especially after an earlier yellow card.
Remove dangerous challenge behaviours from training standards.

tactical_card_risks: entering or leaving field without permission where applicable
training_applications: Teach pressing footwork before tackle selection.
Use constraints that reward delay and channeling, not only winning the ball.
Simulate yellow-card game states to adjust duel risk.
Review penalty-area defending with arm position and body orientation.

technical_models.name: Formation, Role Numbering, and Phase Shape Model
technical_models.purpose: Represent nominal formations, conventional role numbers, and phase-specific shape changes.
technical_models.numbering_convention_note: Position numbers are coaching vocabulary and may vary by country, team, and system. They are not shirt-number laws and are not fixed tactical obligations.

common_role_numbers.role: right back or right outside back
left back or left outside back
centre back or holding midfielder depending on convention

primary_spaces: central lane ahead of centre backs

watchouts: single pivot exposure if eights are high

common_formations.base_lines: 4 defenders, double pivot, 3 attacking midfielders, 1 striker
3 centre backs, wing-backs, 3 central midfielders, 2 forwards
watchouts: wide defending if wing-backs are pinned deep

common_formations.base_lines: 3 centre backs, wing-backs, 2 central midfielders, front 3

technical_models.name: Teaching Progression for Rules to Game Model
technical_models.purpose: Sequence rule learning into tactical behaviour by development level.

learning_goals: Know field landmarks and basic restarts.
Play to whistle and recognise whole-ball-out.
Avoid basic fouls and learn safe tackling posture.
Understand simple positions: goalkeeper, defender, midfielder, forward.
Apply thirds and channels to build, progress, create, and defend.
Use common formations and role numbers.
Make timed runs and recognise offside exceptions.
Choose between counter-press and recovery after loss.
Execute direct/indirect free kick, corner, throw-in, and goal-kick routines.
Operate from a full game model with phase-specific principles.
Change shape by phase and match state.
Manage pressing intensity, tactical fouls, card risk, and penalty-area defending.
Plan substitution and extra-time strategy against physical load.
Use performance data by phase, position, and tactical role rather than raw distance alone.
practice_examples: match-state blocks with scoreline and card constraints
high press to counterpress to rest-defence sequences

technical_models.name: Physical Demands by Rule and Phase
technical_models.purpose: Link laws, phases, formations, and tactics to load exposure.

load_drivers.effect: Extends total exposure and late fatigue, especially when added time is substantial or extra time is possible.
Larger and wider fields can increase running distances and recovery distances; smaller spaces can increase accelerations, decelerations, duels, and rapid decisions.
High press and counter-press increase repeated accelerations, short sprints, and recovery runs.
Frequent turnovers increase high-intensity actions and cognitive load.

Wing-backs and wide forwards often cover repeated high-speed wide runs; central midfielders often accumulate large total and multi-directional load; centre backs often face aerial duels, accelerations, and emergency sprints.
Dead-ball pauses reduce continuous running but add jumps, wrestling/contact, high-force accelerations, and second-ball reactions.

tactical_rules.principle: Time depth runs relative to the ball and second-last opponent.
tactical_rules.tactical_decision: Delay or curve the run until the passer can release; use third-player movement and blindside starting positions to threaten behind without becoming active from offside.
rule_constraints: offside position only matters in opponents' half
hands and arms are excluded from offside position
direct receipt from goal kick, throw-in, or corner cannot be offside

teaching_progression.beginner: Freeze moments to show onside versus offside.
teaching_progression.intermediate: Add pass timing and curved runs.
teaching_progression.advanced: Train line manipulation, delayed runs, and VAR-era body-position discipline.

tactical_rules.principle: A high defensive line compresses the pitch but creates space behind.
tactical_rules.tactical_decision: Use a high line when pressure on the ball is strong; drop or cover when the opponent can play forward unopposed.
rule_constraints: offside can protect the line only when attackers are ahead of the ball and second-last opponent
goalkeeper must be ready to defend space behind

teaching_progression.advanced: Coordinate press trigger, goalkeeper starting position, and centre-back body orientation.

tactical_rules.principle: Pressing must force decisions without reckless or excessive-force contact.
tactical_rules.tactical_decision: Angle the press to remove central passing lanes, arrive under control, and choose delay or tackle based on cover.
rule_constraints: careless contact gives a direct free kick or penalty
reckless challenges are cautions
excessive force is a send-off

teaching_progression.intermediate: Force play one way while staying balanced.
teaching_progression.advanced: Use pressing traps while managing card and set-piece risk.

tactical_rules.principle: Defending inside the penalty area requires lower-risk body and arm positions.
tactical_rules.tactical_decision: Delay and block shooting lanes without lunging, pulling, pushing, or making the body unnaturally bigger with arms.
rule_constraints: direct free kick offences by defenders in their own penalty area become penalties
handball interpretations make arm position and body movement important

teaching_progression.intermediate: Block with arms controlled and feet active.
teaching_progression.advanced: Teach shot-block profiles, cutback defending, and opponent manipulation without fouling.

tactical_rules.principle: Goal kicks are both a possession opportunity and a pressing trigger.
tactical_rules.tactical_decision: Choose short build, third-player escape, or longer distribution based on opponent press, goalkeeper skill, player spacing, and risk near goal.
rule_constraints: ball is in play when kicked and clearly moves
opponents must be outside penalty area until ball is in play
latest law text includes goal-kick delay countdown protocol requiring edition verification

teaching_progression.beginner: Place ball correctly and play to a free teammate.
teaching_progression.intermediate: Create passing triangles with goalkeeper, centre backs, full-backs, and pivot.
teaching_progression.advanced: Use opponent press shape to decide short build, clipped pass, or direct play while maintaining rest defence.

tactical_rules.principle: Throw-ins are high-frequency possession restarts, not pauses.
tactical_rules.tactical_decision: Use pre-planned support angles, movement, and counterpress coverage to retain possession or gain territory.
rule_constraints: thrower must use both hands from behind and over head
opponents must be 2 m from point on touchline
no direct goal from throw-in
thrower cannot touch again before another player

teaching_progression.beginner: Legal throw mechanics and simple support.
teaching_progression.advanced: Use throw-in pressing traps, rotations, and no-offside direct receipt.

tactical_rules.principle: Every attacking set piece needs an anti-counterattack structure.
tactical_rules.tactical_decision: Balance box occupation with players positioned for second balls and immediate counterpress or recovery.
rule_constraints: direct free kicks and corners can score directly
indirect free kicks require another touch
opponents have distance rights but ball becomes live when kicked and clearly moves

teaching_progression.intermediate: Assign delivery, runners, blockers within law, and edge players.
teaching_progression.advanced: Use opposition counter profile to choose rest-defence numbers and marking zones.

tactical_rules.principle: After losing possession, the team must choose counter-press or recover based on ball pressure, numbers, and space behind.
tactical_rules.tactical_decision: If closest players can surround and stop forward play, counter-press; if not, delay and recover into compact shape.
rule_constraints: reckless tactical fouls create card risk
advantage can allow the opponent to continue after a foul
offside line and goalkeeper position must account for space behind

teaching_progression.intermediate: First defender presses while others cover and recover.
teaching_progression.advanced: Use rest-defence structure to determine whether to hunt, delay, or drop.

tactical_rules.principle: A regain can become a fast attack or secure possession depending on opponent balance.
tactical_rules.tactical_decision: First look forward for depth or weak-side space; if forward play is blocked or counterpress is strong, secure possession and build.
rule_constraints: offside applies to team-mate forward passes but not direct receipts from selected restarts
advantage may preserve attacking momentum after opponent fouls

teaching_progression.beginner: Look forward after winning the ball.
teaching_progression.intermediate: Choose dribble, pass forward, or secure based on pressure.
teaching_progression.advanced: Train 5-to-10 second chance creation windows and rest-defence behind the counter.

tactical_rules.principle: Substitution rules create tactical and physical resource constraints.
tactical_rules.tactical_decision: Use substitutions to change role matchups, protect injured or cautioned players, sustain pressing, prepare set pieces, and manage extra-time risk.
rule_constraints: competition rules define substitute count
five-substitute top-level format typically limits opportunities to three plus half-time
extra-time substitution allowances depend on competition rules

teaching_progression.intermediate: Know substitution windows and position coverage.
teaching_progression.advanced: Model substitution timing against fatigue, scoreline, cards, set-piece roles, and penalty shoot-out eligibility.

tactical_rules.principle: A compact block can control central space and force play wide.
tactical_rules.game_moment: out of possession mid or low block
tactical_rules.tactical_decision: Keep horizontal and vertical distances compact, screen central passes, and shift together so wide play becomes predictable.
rule_constraints: penalty-area fouls are high cost
corners and wide free kicks may be conceded if pressure is mistimed
offside line depth affects space behind

teaching_progression.intermediate: Shift as a unit and protect the middle.
teaching_progression.advanced: Use pressing triggers from compact shape and attack quickly after regain.

tactical_rules.principle: Extra time changes risk appetite, physical pacing, and substitution value.
tactical_rules.tactical_decision: Decide whether to chase the game, protect for penalties, or use set pieces as lower-open-play-load chance sources.
rule_constraints: extra time is two equal periods not exceeding 15 minutes each when used
penalty shoot-out eligibility depends on players on the field or temporarily off at the end
sent-off players cannot take part in shoot-out

teaching_progression.beginner: Understand that knockout games may continue.
teaching_progression.intermediate: Practice late-game restart and penalty routines.
teaching_progression.advanced: Build scenario plans for fatigue, cramp, card risk, and penalty takers.

physical_demands.description: Football requires repeated intermittent work over two 45-minute halves plus added time, with possible extra time in knockout formats.
physical_demands.position_notes: Outfield players accumulate most locomotor load; goalkeepers have lower total distance but high reactivity, jumping, diving, distribution, and short acceleration demands.
physical_demands.training_considerations: Blend aerobic capacity, repeated high-intensity ability, football-specific decision-making, and recovery between intense bouts.

physical_demands.description: Total team distance is relatively stable compared with high-intensity and sprint distance, which vary more by match context, tactics, player role, and opposition.
physical_demands.position_notes: Wide players, full-backs, wing-backs, and forwards often face repeated high-speed exposures; central midfielders often combine large total volume with multi-directional actions.
physical_demands.training_considerations: Avoid universal thresholds without context; individualise sprint and high-speed exposure and interpret data by tactical role.

physical_demands.description: Pressing, marking, changing direction, stopping, and restarting create frequent accelerations and decelerations that may not be captured by distance totals alone.
physical_demands.position_notes: Midfielders and defenders often complete many short accelerations and braking actions; wide players add high-speed entries and recovery runs.
physical_demands.training_considerations: Progress deceleration mechanics, eccentric strength, re-acceleration, and change-of-direction quality under decision constraints.

physical_demands.description: Transitions compress decision time and often demand immediate pressure, sprint support, recovery runs, or forward runs into space.
physical_demands.position_notes: Forwards and wide players often sprint forward after regain; defenders and pivots must counterpress, delay, or recover to protect central space.
physical_demands.training_considerations: Condition practices with immediate post-turnover tasks, short reaction windows, and clear decision rules for counter-press versus recovery.

physical_demands.description: Formation and role assignments redistribute physical load even when the same players are on the field.
physical_demands.position_notes: Wing-backs may face repeated end-to-end wide runs; pivots require frequent scanning and short support actions; centre backs face sprint recovery behind high lines.
physical_demands.training_considerations: Profile load by tactical role, not only by generic position label.

physical_demands.description: Set pieces add jumping, wrestling/contact, blocking, sprint starts, and second-ball reactions while also creating brief recovery pauses from open-play running.
physical_demands.position_notes: Centre backs, strikers, and goalkeepers often carry higher aerial and contact demand; edge players and rest-defence players face sprint transition demand.
physical_demands.training_considerations: Include set-piece blocks, landings, aerial timing, and immediate transition actions in load planning.

physical_demands.description: Extra time extends neuromuscular and cognitive fatigue after normal time, raising the importance of substitution planning, hydration, pacing, and penalty preparation.
physical_demands.position_notes: Players with high sprint roles or previous overload may decline sharply; goalkeepers face penalty-specific explosive and perceptual demands.
physical_demands.training_considerations: Prepare late-game scenarios, fatigue-state skill execution, and penalty routines under pressure.

physical_demands.description: Rules and tactics create continuous cognitive load: players scan for offside, pressure, teammate support, referee signals, restart mechanics, card risk, and match state while physically active.
physical_demands.position_notes: Midfielders and goalkeepers often process the largest field picture; defenders must manage line height, opponent runs, and penalty-area risk.
physical_demands.training_considerations: Use representative practices with scanning, communication, and rule constraints rather than isolated conditioning only.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Hamstring strain risk from sprint and high-speed exposure
injury_or_load_risks.mechanism: Fast running places high eccentric demand on hamstrings, especially with sudden spikes, fatigue, poor preparation, or return-to-play gaps.
rule_or_tactical_links: offside and high defensive lines increase sprint races behind
counter-attacks and recovery runs create maximal or near-maximal sprint actions
extra time and added time extend fatigue exposure
mitigation: monitor acute changes in high-speed and sprint load

injury_or_load_risks.mechanism: Repeated pressing, braking, cutting, and re-accelerating create high mechanical load on muscles, tendons, and joints.
rule_or_tactical_links: high press and counter-press require rapid close-downs
small-sided drills can overload deceleration density
restart second balls create explosive stop-start demands
mitigation: alternate high-density pressing days with recovery
use small-sided games carefully in congested weeks

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Contact injuries from tackles, aerial duels, and set-piece congestion
injury_or_load_risks.mechanism: Player-to-player collisions, poor landing mechanics, reckless challenges, and crowded penalty-area marking can produce acute injury and disciplinary sanctions.
rule_or_tactical_links: reckless and excessive-force challenges are carded
corner and free-kick routines concentrate bodies in the box
penalty-area fouls carry high tactical cost
mitigation: teach safe tackling and aerial technique
remove dangerous challenge behaviour from sessions

injury_or_load_risks.mechanism: Rapid growth, incomplete strength development, and sudden increases in match or training intensity can raise vulnerability to overuse and acute injuries.
rule_or_tactical_links: small-sided youth modifications change field size, player numbers, and load density
adult-like pressing demands may exceed youth readiness
competition schedules can compress recovery
mitigation: progressive strength, balance, agility, and landing work
avoid adult tactical load copied directly into youth sessions

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Goalkeeper-specific collision, landing, shoulder, hip, and reactive-load risk
injury_or_load_risks.mechanism: Diving, jumping, landing, distribution, 1v1 saves, and space-behind defending create distinct loads despite lower running totals.
rule_or_tactical_links: goalkeeper is required role
goalkeeper handling rules affect distribution timing
high defensive line increases sweeper actions

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Decision fatigue and rule-error risk late in matches
injury_or_load_risks.mechanism: Fatigue can impair judgement, increasing mistimed tackles, offside errors, restart mistakes, poor scanning, and substitution delays.
rule_or_tactical_links: added time and extra time extend decision load
yellow-card status changes defensive risk
penalty shoot-outs require composure after fatigue

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Underprepared return to match speed after injury or reduced minutes
injury_or_load_risks.mechanism: Players returning without exposure to match-like sprint, deceleration, duel, and cognitive demands may tolerate training but fail under match transitions.
rule_or_tactical_links: substitute appearances can require immediate high-intensity actions
late-game transition chaos can exceed controlled rehab demands
role changes may add unfamiliar running patterns
mitigation: progress sprint and deceleration under decision pressure
coordinate medical, S&C, and coach plans

training_implications.coaching_objective: Give players usable rule understanding: field lines, goals, fouls, restarts, offside basics, and play to whistle.
training_implications.practice_design: Use short small-sided games. Stop briefly after natural restarts and ask players to name the restart, location, and first action.
assessment_cues: Can identify throw-in, goal kick, corner, kick-off, and free kick.
Can explain whole ball out.
Can avoid basic pushing, tripping, and handling.

training_implications.coaching_objective: Teach goalkeeper, defender, midfielder, and forward roles before detailed formations.
training_implications.practice_design: Use lanes or thirds with simple occupation targets: one player wide, one central support, one depth option.
assessment_cues: Players can spread out in possession.
Players can recover between ball and goal after loss.
Players understand that the goalkeeper has special handling rules.

training_implications.coaching_objective: Build safe tackling, balance, landing, and respect for contact rules.
training_implications.practice_design: Teach 1v1 channel defending with speed control, side-on body position, and no slide tackling until players demonstrate control.
assessment_cues: Player slows before challenge.
Player stays balanced and avoids arms/pushes.
Player can delay instead of diving in.

training_implications.coaching_objective: Help players link field zones to tactical decisions: build in defensive third, progress in middle third, create in attacking third.
training_implications.practice_design: Run directional possession through thirds with wide channels, limiting some players to zones to create overload/underload learning.
assessment_cues: Players can identify when to switch play.
Full-backs and midfielders choose based on defender pressure.
Team keeps rest defence behind the ball.

training_implications.coaching_objective: Move from legal mechanics to tactical routines for throw-ins, goal kicks, free kicks, and corners.
training_implications.practice_design: Practice each restart with three options: retain, progress, or attack; always include transition-defence roles.
assessment_cues: Players know required distances and ball-in-play condition.
Players react immediately once ball is live.
Team has assigned second-ball and rest-defence players.

training_implications.coaching_objective: Teach attackers to threaten behind while staying eligible and defenders to move as a line.
training_implications.practice_design: Use 7v7 or 9v9 directional games with a marked offside line, then progress to assistant-referee style live decisions.
assessment_cues: Runs start from onside positions.
Passer and runner coordinate timing.
Defensive line steps or drops together.

training_implications.coaching_objective: Teach the first decision after possession changes: counter-press, recover, counter-attack, or secure.
training_implications.practice_design: Use possession games with immediate transition goals and coach the nearest-player reaction plus support roles.
assessment_cues: Closest player reacts within first seconds.
Team-mates compact or support forward quickly.
Players choose forward pass only when it is available.

training_implications.coaching_objective: Condition players through game actions rather than isolated running only.
training_implications.practice_design: Alternate larger transition games for high-speed exposure with smaller pressing games for acceleration/deceleration load.
assessment_cues: Players repeat efforts without losing shape.
Players recover tactically after high-intensity actions.
Load is progressed rather than spiked.

training_implications.coaching_objective: Define phase-specific principles, role behaviours, formation morphing, restart plans, and match-state rules.
training_implications.practice_design: Use 11v11 phase-of-play blocks with scripted starts: goal kick under high press, attacking-third loss, mid-block regain, late lead, and extra-time fatigue.
assessment_cues: Team shape changes by phase without confusion.
Players know role-specific cues and constraints.
Game model survives opponent and match-state changes.

training_implications.coaching_objective: Teach how laws shape pressing, fouling, offside, goalkeeper play, substitutions, restarts, and extra-time risk.
training_implications.practice_design: Create match-state games with referee constraints: one centre back on yellow, opponent no-offside throw-in, indirect free kick near goal, added-time lead, or extra-time substitution limit.
assessment_cues: Players adjust duel risk on cards.
Team uses legal restart advantages.
Players manage clock and scoreline without losing tactical discipline.

training_implications.coaching_objective: Interpret physical data by tactical role, possession phase, and match context.
training_implications.practice_design: Tag practice blocks by phase and expected load: build-up pressure, high press, counter-attack, low block, set-piece repeat, and extra-time simulation.
assessment_cues: Training load reflects tactical plan.
High-speed and sprint exposure is individualised.
Pressing and deceleration density are monitored.

training_implications.coaching_objective: Integrate injury prevention into warm-up, strength, sprint exposure, landing mechanics, and tactical load design.
training_implications.practice_design: Use structured warm-ups, eccentric hamstring work, sprint exposure, deceleration progressions, and session plans that avoid sudden load spikes before congested match periods.
assessment_cues: Players complete warm-up consistently.
High-risk roles receive appropriate exposure and recovery.
Return-to-play players meet role-specific demands before full match load.
